Dropped: the Nvidia/Jensen Huang cluster, Anthropic IPO and chip funding (no bearing on creative work), Creative Bloq deals, reviews and gadgets, event and webinar announcements, Roastbrief press releases. Considered and left out: Caixa rebrand, Mars on agentic shopping, Sitting Wren, Johnnie Walker, Harry Potter posters, Google Tabletop. Feeds export.arxiv.org and userresearchstrategist.com failed.

stories.title: One prototype that travels from code to Figma and back
stories.blurb: Christine Vallaure keeps the canvas for what a prompt box does badly: putting versions side by side. She cites a Stanford study in which designers who compared several versions made better work than those refining one. The round trip only holds if the Figma component carries the exact name and properties of the code component.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: In-system design: from code to Figma and back. Prototyping in your real design system
sources.author: Christine Vallaure

stories.title: Design exploration, read as a search algorithm
stories.blurb: Matt Ström-Awn asks why some designers keep hundreds of variants in view and others a few artboards, and answers with computer science: depth-first, breadth-first, then beam search, which scores candidates and keeps only the best few. His framing is that product design looks more like chess than a Rubik’s cube, with hundreds of dimensions and expensive evaluation.

stories.title: Usage-based AI pricing turns cost into a design material
stories.blurb: Arin Bhowmick lists what he treats as non-negotiable: the estimate next to the button, a confirmation before expensive tasks, cost per task, early warnings and user-set caps. His own addition is to translate credits into work, such as “enough for about three more prototypes”, and to give each AI feature a cost budget before it is built.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: Every click has a price now. Who designs how that “feels”?
sources.author: Arin Bhowmick

stories.title: Research platforms make method decisions most teams never review
stories.blurb: Saeideh Bakhshi walks through where tools decide for the researcher: which study designs are possible, who gets recruited and excluded, what counts as task success. A platform without randomization or counterbalancing quietly changes what a comparison can conclude. Her ask is to evaluate a tool’s methods with the scrutiny applied to one’s own research.

sources.name: Saeideh Bakhshi
sources.headline: The Research Tooling Industry Is Selling Us Methodological Shortcuts
sources.author: Saeideh Bakhshi

stories.title: Koto hides a signpost in the Giffgaff wordmark and builds the system on it
stories.blurb: The final f now ends in a pointed tip, and that arrow recurs across the identity to point at prices and offers. The brief was the usual challenger problem: evolve for a crowded market without losing the personality people signed up for.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Koto points Giffgaff towards its next chapter with a signpost-led rebrand

stories.title: HOW+HOW gives Pets a brand architecture for insurance, a kids club and a foundation
stories.blurb: Each sub-brand gets its own positioning, verbal identity and visual system, tied to the masterbrand by shared devices. Pet Pals is built like an animated series around a character called Pogo, the Foundation uses fluid vector paths the studio calls zoomies.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: HOW+HOW creates unified sub-brand system for pet retailer Pets

stories.title: Ironman’s women’s community becomes Woven, with a tone that skips the cheerleading
stories.blurb: Essential Viewing handled naming, strategy, identity, tone of voice, merch and launch campaign. Three chevrons for swim, bike and run interlock into a W, the campaign line is “I Am Not One Thing”, and the grainy gradients borrow from 90s UK garage rather than sports branding.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: This identity for a women s sports community swaps cheerleading for real talk

stories.title: AI job interviewers are brand touchpoints, and people film themselves trolling them
stories.blurb: Clips of candidates baiting interview avatars reach millions of views, and the audience attaches a logo whether or not the system is verified, as with an unconfirmed Burger King clip. State of Brand’s argument: automating an interaction makes it matter more, because a bad default hits every candidate, and an avatar’s irritated mood is a product decision someone made.

sources.name: State of Brand
sources.headline: Your AI Interviewer Is Now a Brand Spokesperson. The Internet Is Testing Its Temper by Trolling It. | State of Brand

stories.title: 19 IGF jurors refuse any game made with generative AI, Big Walk discloses ten lines
stories.blurb: The jurors want the festival to ban games containing any AI-generated work. House House then disclosed that LLMs were used sparingly on Big Walk, for a Unity shadow bug among other things, amounting to well under 0.1% of the code. The case shows how little room the disclosure debate leaves between none and some.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: The indie game community is in disarray over AI and Big Walk

stories.title: Adobe Sneaks: explorable photos, characters directed by talking, edits that copy themselves
stories.blurb: Sight Span turns a flat image into a 3D space to pick a new angle from, Screen Test shapes an AI character in an audition-style conversation, Rinse Repeat applies a retouch to other subjects in the same photo. Scene Sweep carries one edit across every shot of a sequence. All of it is experimental, with no word on if or where it ships.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: 5 wild Adobe Sneaks that creatives need to know about

stories.title: Photoshop 2027 gets layer-based Relight and Restyle, Premiere gets the Creative Agent
stories.blurb: Relight places up to three virtual lights, Generative Restyle has a strength slider, and both stay editable as layers. In beta: a tool that turns flattened graphics such as a flyer or PDF into editable layers. Premiere generates video, sound and music in the timeline and opens to third-party models such as Kling and Seedance.

sources.headline: Adobe unveils Photoshop 2027 with a host of new AI features
